subject: Bootstrapping for the standard error of an indirect effect and finding bias-corrected confidence intervals.

messages.author: 4880b1699141a832
messages.subject: Bootstrapping for the standard error of an indirect effect and finding bias-corrected confidence intervals.
parts:
Hello all, 

I am running a model using sem() in R. There are no latent variables, the basic structure looks something like:

my.model <- '
                      y1 ~ a*x1 + b*x2 + c*t
                      t ~ d*x1 + e*x2
'
fit <- sem(model=my.model, data=my.data, method='MLR', sampling.weights='Weight')

I am interested in the indirect effect of x1 and x2 through t on y1. The problem I have is that my dataset has sampling weights that I am required to use. It seems that with sampling weights used, it is impossible for me to use a method that will allow me to generate bootstrapped standard errors for the indirect effects of x1 and x2, and then without the bootstrapped standard errors, I cannot obtain bias-corrected confidence intervals.

Is there a way for me to do this? The alternative would be using the Sobel test statistic  and assuming a standard Normal distribution if I'm not mistaken, but there seems to be a great deal of literature on how this is not a good approach to inference on the coefficient attached to the indirect effect, so I was hoping for some advice on this.

Thank you, 
Khusro

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Bootstrapping for the standard error of an indirect effect and finding bias-corrected confidence intervals.
parts:
I would try fitting the model with and without weights.

If the weights don't make much difference (and they usually don't), remove them and bootstrap it.

Jeremy

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: Bootstrapping for the standard error of an indirect effect and finding bias-corrected confidence intervals.
parts:
How about the Monte Carlo function from semTools?

https://rdrr.io/cran/semTools/man/monteCarloCI.html

The example in the help page is one for indirect effect. I haven't used this function and also haven't used sampling weights but, according to the help page, it will work as long as you can get the VCOV.

-- Shu Fai
